title: Updating a normalized Boolean block
statement: Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $x\colon\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, choose a row $i$, a column $j$, and a Boolean value $b$. Encode each Boolean by $\sigma(\mathrm{false})=1$ and $\sigma(\mathrm{true})=-1$, and define $S(x)_k=(\sum_{l=1}^m\sigma(x_{kl}))/\sqrt m$, with real division interpreted in the usual way, including when $m=0$. If $x'$ is obtained by replacing the entry $x_{ij}$ by $b$, then $S(x')=S(x)+\frac{\sigma(b)-\sigma(x_{ij})}{\sqrt m}e_i$, where $e_i$ is the vector equal to $1$ in coordinate $i$ and $0$ elsewhere.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is a Boolean array indexed by rows and columns
replaced: For $n,m\ge0$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times m}$, define $S_m(x)_k=m^{-1/2}\sum_{l=1}^m(-1)^{x_{kl}}$, interpreting division by zero as zero. If $x^{ij\leftarrow b}$ replaces bit $(i,j)$ by $b$, then $S_m(x^{ij\leftarrow b})=S_m(x)+\bigl((-1)^b-(-1)^{x_{ij}}\bigr)m^{-1/2}e_i$, where $e_i$ is the $i$th coordinate vector.
